newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Schiphol passenger/cargo traffic up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Schiphol passenger/cargo traffic up in 1996.

text.p: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport said on Friday its passenger and cargo traffic increased around 10 percent in 1996 from the previous year.

Passengers passing through the airport rose by 9.6 percent to 27.8 million, while cargo traffic saw a rise of 10.8 percent to 1.08 million tonnes during the year, the airport said in its annual results statement.
On the passenger side, the Dutch airport further increased its market share in Europe.

Of the ten leading European passenger airports, Schipol had an 8.7 percent market share, compared to 8.4 percent in 1995. It now holds fourth place after London Heathrow, Frankfurt and Paris Charles de Gaulle, it said.
It was now also Europe's second largest cargo airport, after Frankfurt, the airport added, surpassing Heathrow during the year.
Of the top ten cargo airports, Schiphol said it had a 15.8 percent market share in 1996. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
